title: Claude spends 3 hours on one prompt and returns a playable spot-the-difference tree game
summary: Simon Willison gave Claude a single prompt in the iPhone app to build a three.js game about appreciating differences between generated trees. Claude worked for over three hours and returned a game with music, animation and achievements.
agent_role: Claude designed and built the whole game from one prompt over a 3-hour-7-minute run; the human only wrote the prompt and published the result.
outcome: Author reports Claude returned a cosy spot-the-difference game with music, animation and achievements that is quite compelling to play.
what_they_did: Simon Willison used the regular Claude iPhone app in chat mode, not Claude Code, with Claude Opus 5.5 Max. He gave it one prompt: build a three.js game called "Tree appreciator" that shows two algorithmically generated trees and is about appreciating their differences, and think hard about making it fun and beautiful. He then published the result.
how_it_went: He reports Claude worked for 3 hours and 7 minutes and returned a cosy spot-the-difference game with music, animation and achievements that is quite compelling to play.
worth_knowing: Willison says that telling the model to "make sure it is fun" works uncomfortably well.
prompt: Build a three.js game called "[game name]" that shows [what the game displays] and whose core mechanic is [the idea, e.g. noticing differences between two generated objects]. Think hard about how to make sure it is both fun and beautiful. Deliver it as a single HTML file I can open in a browser, and briefly explain the game rules and controls when you are done.

curation.rationale: A working, playable result with a shared transcript and a notable 3-hour autonomous run from a single prompt, but it is another agent-built game with little process detail.
